record.original_question: For a weighted Hardy space H^2_omega, is there a characterization of a function f whose polynomial multiples are dense in the space that relies on the behavior of the zeros of the optimal polynomial approximants to 1/f?

evidence.quote: A function f in H^2_omega is called cyclic if its polynomial multiples are dense in the space.

Given a function f in H^2_omega not identically 0 and n in N, we define the n-th optimal polynomial approximant of 1/f in H^2_omega to be the polynomial q_n that minimizes ||pf - 1||_omega among all polynomials p of degree at most n.

Open Question 3. For a given space H^2_omega (or, say for the Bergman space A^2 or the classical Dirichlet space D), is there a characterization of a cyclic function f that relies on the behavior of the zeros of the opas for 1/f?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega = (\omega_k)_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence of positive weights with $\omega_0 = 1$, and define the weighted Hardy space
$$H^2_\omega = \Big\{ f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k z^k \text{ holomorphic on } \mathbb{D} : \|f\|_\omega^2 := \sum_{k=0}^\infty |a_k|^2 \omega_k < \infty \Big\},$$
assumed to contain the polynomials as a dense subset and such that the shift $f(z)\mapsto zf(z)$ is bounded. A function $f \in H^2_\omega$ is called cyclic if the set $\{p f : p \in \mathbb{C}[z]\}$ of its polynomial multiples is dense in $H^2_\omega$. For $f \in H^2_\omega$ with $f\not\equiv 0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th optimal polynomial approximant (opa) of $1/f$ in $H^2_\omega$ is the unique polynomial $q_n$ of degree at most $n$ that minimizes
$$\|p f - 1\|_\omega \quad \text{among all polynomials } p \text{ with } \deg p \le n.$$
Provide a characterization of the cyclic functions $f \in H^2_\omega$ purely in terms of the behavior (e.g., location, distribution, or limiting set) of the zeros of the optimal polynomial approximants $q_n$ of $1/f$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, do so in the special cases of the Bergman space $A^2$ (weights $\omega_k = 1/(k+1)$) and the classical Dirichlet space $\mathcal{D}$ (weights $\omega_k = k+1$).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2022–2025) has obtained partial results about the asymptotic distribution and equidistribution of zeros of optimal polynomial approximants and their relationship to cyclicity in Bergman, Dirichlet, and $\ell^p_A$ spaces, but a complete characterization of cyclic functions in $H^2_\omega$ (or in $A^2$ or $\mathcal{D}$) purely via the behavior of opa zeros has not been established. The question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution of zeros of some polynomials related to cyclic functions
status_evidence.snippet: For some subsequence, the zeros of {1 - p_n f} are asymptotically equidistributed on the unit circle.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on zero distribution related to cyclicity exist but do not give a full characterization.

status_evidence.title: Zeros of optimal polynomial approximants in ℓ^p_A
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of the location of opa zeros in ℓ^p_A spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Active research provides bounds and properties of opa zeros, but no general characterization of cyclicity in H^2_omega via opa zeros.

status_evidence.title: Metric projections, zeros of optimal polynomial approximants, and some extremal problems in Hardy spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate properties of zeros of opas.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of characterizing cyclic functions via opa zeros remains a topic of ongoing investigation.
